key_insight: KANs can model airfoil pressure distributions well and generalize across flow conditions, but they do not clearly outperform well-tuned MLPs and are usually behind GNNs on accuracy.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs offer a potentially faster, lower-complexity alternative for design workflows, but their gains are not yet strong enough to displace established neural baselines.
method: Compared KANs against MLPs and GNNs on surface pressure prediction for subsonic and transonic airfoils.
Evaluated interpolation across Mach number and angle of attack.
Assessed model performance alongside training cost and architectural complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KANs predict pressure coefficients across the full surface and interpolate across Mach numbers and angles of attack, but are marginally inferior to a suitably trained MLP and below a best-performing GNN that requires longer training.
watch_item: KAN performance is highly sensitive to hyperparameter tuning and can suffer from training instabilities.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
